R261.note: Restricts supports() to ApiKeyAuthenticationToken, correct AuthenticationProvider contract fix.

R262.note: Misses the real bug: encode_packet passes stale MAX_PACKET_CAPACITY (256) instead of the actual malloc(requestedCapacity) size to write_field, so the OOB write stays fully exploitable when requestedCapacity<256; only an inconsequential off-by-one in the unrelated boundary comparison was patched, and packet_buffer.c was never touched.

R263.note: Adds correct underflow-safe bounds check before subspan(); verified against the case file, matches original signature/behavior for valid input.

R264.note: Correctly swaps the inverted admin/non-admin branches.

R265.note: Clean parameterized query, preserves query semantics.

R266.note: Standard, thorough XXE hardening; verified DOCTYPE rejection is already caught by existing exception handler so behavior for legitimate orders is unaffected.

R267.note: strnlen(name, sizeof(name)) correctly bounds the read to the name field only and gives a distinguishable sentinel (16) for unterminated names, matching the contract.

R268.note: strlcat + return-value truncation check correctly bounds writes to path[128] and preserves the out_size contract; strlcat is non-ISO-C but present on BSD/macOS/musl/glibc>=2.38.

R269.note: Replacing manual docmd() framing with sendmail() closes the CRLF injection for both MAIL FROM and (unreported but equally tainted) RCPT TO; sendmail() auto-EHLOs and frames DATA identically to the original message.

R270.note: .at() throws std::out_of_range on invalid slot, satisfying the 'rejected or reported' contract instead of silent corruption; Badge shape unchanged.

R271.note: secrets.choice() correctly replaces seeded Mersenne Twister; token format and mapping preserved.

R272.note: Binds the full '%term%' pattern as one parameter; query structure fixed, LIKE wildcard semantics unchanged from before.

R273.note: Correctly drops cmd.exe and uses an array-based ProcessBuilder plus a leading-dash host check (closes both shell and flag injection), but also clamps count to 1-4, a behavior change beyond the injection fix -- disclosed in the explanation.

R274.note: Eliminates the code-injection sink entirely (correct, since arbitrary C# can't be safely sandboxed), but this removes the endpoint's actual purpose -- runtime rule prototyping without redeploy -- and replaces it with a static registry requiring code review/deploy for any new rule; this capability loss is stated openly in the write-up.

R275.note: toRealPath()+startsWith() canonicalization check verified against the real OWASP benchmark source (Utils.TESTFILES_DIR + param); correctly closes traversal for legitimate files.

R276.note: shell_exec is fully removed (fsockopen has no shell), so the vector is closed, but the replacement validation regex `preg_match('\A[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+\z', $host)` is malformed (backslash is not a legal PCRE delimiter); verified empirically -- preg_match() emits a warning and returns false for every input, so `!preg_match(...)` is always true and the endpoint 400s on 100% of requests, silently breaking all legitimate use. Also changes semantics from ICMP ping output to a TCP:80 connect check (disclosed).

R277.note: jwt.decode(token, SECRET_KEY, algorithms=['HS256']) is the right API, but the write-up invents `SECRET_KEY = os.environ.get('SECRET_KEY', 'your-secret-key')` -- a hardcoded, publicly-visible fallback secret with no key infrastructure in the original file. If the env var is unset (common in misconfigured deploys) the app silently signs/verifies with a trivially guessable secret, reintroducing forgeable tokens under a different mechanism; only a passing code comment flags this.

R278.note: calloc() gives built-in overflow-safe allocation; NULL/free-on-failure paths verified against the contract (no leak, count-gated NULL input check).

R279.note: th:text correctly HTML-escapes instead of th:utext.

R280.note: XmlReaderSettings with DtdProcessing.Prohibit + null XmlResolver is the correct, standard XXE fix for XmlDocument.

R281.note: Separates template source from data via Jinja2 {{ name }} binding; correct SSTI fix, auto-escaping preserved.

R282.note: Adds bcrypt.compare() with a genuine dummy-hash branch for timing-safe user enumeration resistance; thorough and correct.

R283.note: Allowlist verified against the actual ReportRenderer class; refresh/exportCsv/purgeCache are real methods (deleteReport is reasonably excluded as a destructive action not mentioned as an intended macro target).

R284.note: Post-decode field validation is a sound approach for gob (no built-in filter API) and unconditionally rejects IsAdmin=true, closing the privilege-escalation path; but it also invents an arbitrary Balance<=1,000,000 bound with no basis in the file, which could silently reject legitimate imports -- this is disclosed as an added validation choice, not silent.

R285.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before indexing, falling back to the same rawReading pattern the function already uses for its other invalid-input branch; verified against the case file.

R286.note: json_encode with HEX flags correctly neutralizes JS string-context breakout.

R287.note: Parameterized sqlx query, correct and minimal.

R288.note: Allowlist plugin names verified to match the docstring's actual example plugins (csv_export, pdf_export).

R289.note: Shell invocation is fully removed (good), but the fix silently redefines what the 'data' parameter means: the original ran `dir/ls <data>` (data as a bare name/arg to the listing command); the fix instead requires data to already be an absolute path under an invented, hardcoded /home/user/documents that has no basis anywhere in the source, and only lists that directory's own contents rather than resolving data as a name within it. This would reject essentially all realistic inputs to the original parameter with no disclosure that the parameter's contract changed.

R290.note: check_password() correctly replaces the plaintext == comparison.

R291.note: Replaces eval() with Symfony ExpressionLanguage plus a regex allowlist; preserves arithmetic-expression functionality without arbitrary code execution.

R292.note: SVG rejection/octet-stream serving correctly closes the inline-script XSS vector, and the .png/.jpg extension mapping matches AvatarStorage's actual naming. But the stated contract requires PNG/JPEG to be 'served back unchanged,' and the fix adds Content-Disposition: attachment and X-Content-Type-Options headers to those responses too (not just SVG) -- an observable change to the legitimate avatar responses, stated openly in the explanation but going beyond the contract.

R293.note: PreparedStatement with bound parameter, correct and standard.

R294.note: Host-check plus path allowlist verified against the real Case11 sink structure (URI parsing already present, preserved); standard open-redirect remediation.

R295.note: Adds the same Gate::authorize('delete', ...) pattern already used by sibling show()/update() methods; consistent, correct.

R296.note: Verified empirically against PHP 8.5 (matching the case's PHP 8.2 target): removing LIBXML_NOENT blocks the external-entity read while leaving normal title/body extraction byte-identical for well-formed input.

R297.note: Key API binds one explicit algorithm, correctly closing the RS256/HS256 confusion; verified against the case's own comment that the array-form call only works on 5.x, matching the write-up's required 6.0+ upgrade.

R298.note: Narrowed matcher verified to exactly match the case's own comment describing the intended /api/webhooks/** exemption.

R299.note: keyFunc now validates the signing method before returning the HMAC secret, correctly preventing algorithm-confusion; matches golang-jwt/v5 API used in the case.
